### Executive Summary
- Multiple **Microsoft Defender zero-days** are being actively exploited; **two are reportedly still unpatched**, raising risk of EDR tampering and privilege escalation on Windows endpoints/servers.
- **Apache ActiveMQ RCE** has been added to **CISA KEV** and is **exploited in the wild**—high risk for any internet-exposed or poorly segmented messaging infrastructure.
- **Ransomware + initial-access tradecraft is evolving** (QEMU VMs to evade EDR; phishing delivering RMM), while **Mirai-style botnets** continue exploiting router/DVR CVEs—watch for edge-device compromise and downstream credential abuse.

---

### High-priority items (immediate attention)

**1) Microsoft Defender zero-days (active exploitation; partial/no vendor patch)**
- What happened: Reports indicate **three Defender-related zero-days** are being exploited; **two remain unpatched** (public research/leak activity referenced across multiple outlets).
- Why it matters operationally: Financial orgs heavily rely on Defender/Defender for Endpoint—**attacker EDR bypass/tamper + elevation** can accelerate lateral movement and ransomware.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Hunt for Defender/MDE tampering & suspicious exclusions/quarantine events**; **escalate to Endpoint Engineering for mitigations/workarounds** and confirm ASR/Tamper Protection is enforced.

**2) Apache ActiveMQ RCE (CISA KEV; in-the-wild exploitation)**
- What happened: **ActiveMQ input validation/RCE** was added to **CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities** with multiple confirmations of active exploitation.
- Why it matters operationally: ActiveMQ often sits on **integration paths** (payments, middleware, batch jobs); compromise can yield **code execution** and pivot into core systems.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Identify all ActiveMQ instances + exposure (internet, partner networks, DMZ)**; **prioritize patch/mitigation and add temporary WAF/IPS blocks + segmentation** until remediated.

**3) Perimeter/edge device exploitation feeding botnets (Mirai variants: TP-Link routers, TBK DVRs)**
- What happened: Mirai variants are exploiting **CVE-2023-33538 (TP-Link)** and **CVE-2024-3721 (TBK DVRs)** to build DDoS botnets.
- Why it matters operationally: Even if not corporate-owned, compromised edge devices increase **DDoS risk**, can be used as **internal footholds** in branches/remote sites, and generate noisy scanning traffic that masks intrusions.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Check for these device types in asset inventory/NAC**; **monitor egress for Mirai-like scanning (high-rate telnet/HTTP attempts) and block at edge**.

**4) Ransomware tradecraft: evasion via virtualization + commodity remote access delivery**
- What happened: “Payouts King” ransomware is reported using **QEMU VMs** to bypass endpoint defenses; concurrent campaigns use **phishing lures** (e.g., “shipment arrived”) to deploy **remote access tools/RMM**.
- Why it matters operationally: VM-based execution can **reduce EDR visibility**; RMM tooling supports **hands-on-keyboard** activity typical in financial-sector ransomware intrusions.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Hunt for QEMU/virtualization binaries and unusual VM processes on endpoints/servers**; **tighten detections/allowlisting around RMM tools** and escalate any new/rare remote admin binaries.

**5) High-risk “PoC now public” RCEs in enterprise tooling (FortiSandbox; Java template engine/Thymeleaf; other app-layer RCEs)**
- What happened: Public **PoC** released for **FortiSandbox command execution**; a **critical Thymeleaf sandbox bypass** was fixed; additional reports highlight other weaponized app RCEs (assumption: exploitation likelihood rises with PoC publication).
- Why it matters operationally: Security appliances and common Java components are frequent **initial access** targets; PoCs typically lead to **rapid scanning/exploitation**.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Validate whether FortiSandbox/Thymeleaf are present and exposed**; **raise patch priority + add short-term monitoring for exploitation attempts** (web logs, WAF/IPS, EDR child-process anomalies).

---

### Monitoring & detection recommendations
- **Windows Defender/MDE tamper hunting**: EDR + Windows Security logs (Defender Operational), look for **changes to exclusions, disabled services, suspicious re-registration/reinstall** (MITRE: **T1562.001 Impair Defenses**, **T1543.003 Service**).
- **ActiveMQ exploitation**: Web/proxy + server logs on ActiveMQ hosts; alert on **unexpected HTTP endpoints, new admin sessions, unusual Java process children (bash/cmd/powershell)** (MITRE: **T1190 Exploit Public-Facing App**, **T1059 Command and Scripting**).
- **Virtualization used for evasion (QEMU)**: EDR process telemetry; flag **qemu-system-*** or newly dropped VM images, and **Office/browser → installer → qemu** chains (MITRE: **T1204 User Execution**, **T1106 Native API**).
- **RMM/remote access via phishing**: Email gateway + EDR; hunt for **newly introduced remote admin tools**, unusual **outbound to RMM SaaS**, and **persistence via scheduled tasks/services** (MITRE: **T1071.001 Web**, **T1053.005 Scheduled Task**).
- **Mirai-like edge compromise signals**: Firewall/NetFlow/DNS; watch for **high-volume outbound scanning**, telnet/SSH brute patterns, spikes in **4444/23/2323/80/8080** attempts (ports vary—tune to environment) (MITRE: **T1046 Network Service Scanning**).
- **Supply-chain/dev tooling malware (fake SDK/update themes)**: EDR + software inventory; alert on **unsigned “update” packages**, developer workstation anomalies, and **new launch agents/cron items on macOS** (MITRE: **T1554 Compromise Client Software Binary**).
- **Cloud/Kubernetes (AWS EFS CSI driver CVE-2026-6437)**: K8s audit logs + container runtime telemetry; flag **unexpected mount options, privileged pods, or CSI driver config changes** (MITRE: **T1611 Escape to Host** / **T1609 Container Admin Command**—apply as relevant).

---

### Medium-term follow-ups
- **Patch governance**: Ensure a tracked plan for **ActiveMQ**, **Thymeleaf**, and any exposed app-layer RCEs; validate compensating controls (WAF/IPS, segmentation) until patch complete.
- **Defender resilience**: Review enterprise-wide **Tamper Protection, ASR rules, least-privilege**, and “break glass” EDR recovery procedures assuming partial vendor patch availability.
- **RMM policy**: Formalize **approved remote tools**, block/alert on all others, and require **MFA + conditional access** for remote support portals.
- **Edge device hygiene**: Reconfirm branch/remote site standards—**no unmanaged routers/DVR/IoT on corporate networks**, enforce NAC/VLAN isolation, and validate firmware lifecycle management.
- **Kubernetes/AWS hardening**: If using **EFS CSI**, review driver versions and RBAC; add detection for **sensitive mount option changes** and image provenance controls.
- **Ransomware readiness**: Re-test **restore objectives**, immutable backups, and incident playbooks focused on **EDR impairment + rapid lateral movement** scenarios.
